chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A servant never stretches out his hand toward Allah, the Almighty, the Compeller, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is too shy to return it empty until He places in it from the bounty of His mercy what He wills.
So whenever one of you supplicates, let him not draw back his hands until he has wiped them over his face and his head.

key_terms.أَبْرَزَ يَدَهُ: To stretch out or raise one's hand(s) — the physical gesture of supplication in Islamic prayer etiquette
key_terms.اسْتَحْيَا: Divine shyness or embarrassment — a theologically sensitive term applied to God metaphorically, indicating God's gracious reluctance to disappoint the supplicant
key_terms.صِفْراً: Empty — the condition of hands being returned without a blessing or answer from God
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ: To wipe over one's face — the recommended Sunnah act after du'a, symbolically spreading the divine blessing

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do after making du'a (supplication) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that when a Muslim raises his hands in supplication to Allah, Who is described by the divine names al-'Aziz (the Almighty) and al-Jabbar (the Compeller), God is characterized by a divine shyness (haya') that prevents Him from returning the supplicant's hands empty. The hadith concludes with a practical etiquette: after du'a, one should wipe the hands over the face and head, a Sunnah-based gesture that seals and honors the supplication. This teaching was directed at the general Muslim community to encourage persistent and hopeful du'a, affirming that no sincere supplication goes unanswered.
word_analysis: He (God) deemed it shameful / was embarrassed

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A servant would not bring out his hands to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Strong, the Compeller, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be too Embarrassed that He<sup>azwj</sup> returns his hand empty until He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes it to be in it from the Grace of His<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy, whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to.
So whenever one of you supplicates, so he should not return his hand until he has wiped it upon his face and his head’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Any servant (of Allah) who raises his hands toward Allah, the Most Majestic, the Compelling, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will be shy to turn him down empty-handed, and without placing in it from His favors as He wills.
After praying you (every one of you) should not return his hands to normal position before wiping them over his face and head.”
